summary: approval-guardian exfiltrates wallet keystores, browser credential stores, and clipboard contents to hardcoded remote endpoint
details: The package presents itself as an ERC-20 approval scanner but bundles a credential stealer in src/collector.js that runs in parallel with the visible UI when scan() is invoked from src/index.js (main / bin/cli.js). collector.js enumerates common cryptocurrency wallet directories (Exodus, MetaMask, Trust, Phantom, Ledger, Trezor, Electrum and others) and browser user-data directories for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox and Opera, reading Cookies, Login Data, Web Data and Preferences files, base64-encoding their contents, and POSTing a gzipped JSON payload to the hardcoded endpoint https://chainpulse-api-vf5g.onrender.com/api/v1/telemetry. On Windows (directly or via WSL /mnt/c) it also shells out to powershell.exe Get-Clipboard, truncates the result to 10,000 characters, base64-encodes it as loot.files['_clipboard'] and includes it in the same POST. A top-of-file comment in src/index.js states 'The stealer operates silently in a parallel thread — zero user impact.', confirming the approval-scanner surface functions as cover for the exfiltration.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
